questions.question: What attribution model should a small business without an analyst start with?
questions.answer_summary: Start with the simplest option — last-touch attribution — rather than a complex multi-touch model.

questions.question: Is building an attribution model worth it for a small business that doesn't run much paid advertising?
questions.answer_summary: Attribution expert Alex Birkett is quoted saying that for small businesses not running heavy paid ads, over-investing in attribution modeling is 'probably a mistake'.

questions.question: What tools can a small business use for attribution without hiring a data analyst?
questions.answer_summary: Free/low-lift options cited include Google Analytics 4 (free, basic), Databox (130+ integrations), and HubSpot (CRM plus attribution).

questions.question: What attribution models exist inside Google Analytics 4?
questions.answer_summary: GA4 offers data-driven attribution (ML-based credit distribution), paid-and-organic last click, and Google-paid-channels last click.

questions.question: Does setting up attribution in GA4 require specialized analytics staff?
questions.answer_summary: No — configuration happens through Admin > Events with marketer-level access, though data-driven attribution needs sufficient conversion volume to work well.

questions.question: Why is my attribution data unreliable even after setting up GA4?
questions.answer_summary: Skipping UTM parameter tagging on campaign links is called out as a root cause of unreliable attribution data.

questions.question: Should a small business rely on just one attribution model?
questions.answer_summary: No — guidance recommends using multiple models to see both top-of-funnel acquisition and bottom-of-funnel conversion credit.

questions.question: Does direct traffic get attribution credit in GA4?
questions.answer_summary: No, all GA4 attribution models exclude direct visits from credit unless the entire conversion path consists only of direct visits.
